analysis.investment_thesis: Wakefit shows genuine revenue momentum (29% CAGR to ₹1,256 Cr) and an attractive 54% gross margin, suggesting real brand value in India's underpenetrated home furnishing market. However, persistent net losses (₹-35 Cr in FY25), a dangerously thin cash balance (₹7 Cr), and rising debt (₹273 Cr) signal that management has not yet converted scale into shareholder value — a critical Fisher prerequisite.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 21–30% annually, meeting Fisher's growth threshold with consistent top-line acceleration.
54% gross margin indicates genuine pricing power and brand differentiation in a commoditized category.
EBITDA improving steadily (₹-87 Cr → ₹56 Cr → ₹83 Cr), showing real operating leverage emerging at scale.
key_risks: Persistent net losses (₹-146, ₹-15, ₹-35 Cr over three years) with no clear profitability inflection — nine years post-founding.
Cash position collapsed to ₹7 Cr against ₹273 Cr debt and ₹30 Cr annual finance costs; liquidity is perilously thin.
Highly competitive D2C home furnishing space with low switching costs; no durable innovation moat evident versus Sleep Company, Urban Ladder, and Pepperfry.
red_flags: ROE of -6.72% and ROCE of -1.05% — both negative. Fisher demands ROE >20% and rising.
Debt nearly doubled in two years (₹144 Cr → ₹273 Cr) while cash fell from ₹62 Cr to ₹7 Cr — deteriorating financial position.
P/E of 118x quoted despite negative net income is a sign of speculative pricing, not earnings quality.
Promoter holding only 37% — low skin-in-the-game for a founder-led D2C brand this early in its journey.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my Scuttlebutt lens, Wakefit has built genuine consumer mindshare in the mattress category with a D2C model, and the 54% gross margin tells me customers accept a price premium — that is a real signal. Revenue compounding at ~29% meets my core growth test, and the EBITDA trend from ₹-87 Cr to ₹+83 Cr over three years shows that operational leverage does exist in the model. I can see the potential of a large, underpenetrated Indian home furnishing market here.

However, my 15-point checklist breaks down badly on financial discipline. After nine years, net losses are widening again (₹-15 → ₹-35 Cr), cash is effectively gone (₹7 Cr), and management is funding growth increasingly with debt — finance costs jumped from ₹13 Cr to ₹30 Cr. I will not own a business where capital returns are negative (ROE -6.72%, ROCE -1.05%) and management cannot demonstrate a credible path to the 20%+ returns on equity I demand. At EV/EBITDA of 55x and P/S of 3.4x for a loss-making company, the market is pricing in perfection I do not yet see in the numbers.
